clue.text: Direct crappy item at the end of the film?

definitions.text: item at the end of the film?

indicators.note: crappy means badly made, so the letters of the word before it are in a mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a poor director whose shoddy item tops off the movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Each name in the closing roll of a film is one entry in the list shown as the picture ends.

clue.text: Plea made by wolf during penetration

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: penetration is entry, the act of going in
to wolf is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of a lecherous man's pleading while making a sexual advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or appeal, a formal word for a plea.

clue.text: Mucky rag, indispensable driving aid?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Daily ..., a British tabloid newspaper, scornfully called a dirty rag
second meaning: the glass a driver checks to see behind the car

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a filthy cloth for wiping a windscreen; a rag here is a low-grade newspaper, and the Mirror is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye mocks the tabloid as grubby, and every car has a reflective glass for rear vision.

clue.text: Royal hanger-on reportedly discovered having one with Brenda

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word for discovered is taken by its sound

parts.note: discovered in the act means caught
I is the Roman numeral for one
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, and ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Gossip that a palace flunkey was found having an affair with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda', so ER (Elizabeth Regina) comes from her name; CAUGHT said aloud gives COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier attends the monarch at court, often seen as a fawning attendant.

clue.text: Toss off White without resistance

indicators.note: off here means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A crude jibe about a man called White pleasuring himself without any effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss off' reads as one phrase, but 'Toss' alone is the definition and 'off' signals the anagram; 'without' here means added on the outside, so R joins WHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss and to writhe both describe twisting and turning restlessly, as in a sleepless bed.

clue.text: Fanny behind this cover-up? Only just

definitions.text: Fanny behind this cover-up? Only just

parts.words: Fanny behind this cover-up? Only just
parts.note: a skimpy undergarment that barely conceals the private parts; fanny is British slang for the female genitals

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang fanny means the vulva, not the buttocks as in America; this tiny garment hides it, but only just.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment is a minimal thong of cloth on a string, worn by dancers and strippers, offering very little coverage.

clue.text: Flaunter's performance in bad taste

definitions.note: read as 'flaunter is', so the definition is the noun flaunter

parts.note: a show is a performance
off means unacceptable, as in 'that remark was a bit off'

explanation.surface: A critic judges an exhibitionist's act to be tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off displays themselves ostentatiously, just as a flaunter parades possessions or talents.

clue.text: Intolerance towards gays, etc. — magnanimous Tory conversion

parts.note: big can mean generous, as in 'that's big of you'

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so the letters of the party member are rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirical hope that a generous-minded Conservative might be converted from his prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is prejudiced hostility to people of a different group, such as homophobia.

clue.text: Referee whom employer would rather was less revealing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally someone who blows a whistle, as a match official does

definitions.text: whom employer would rather was less revealing
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an insider who exposes wrongdoing at the firm

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal and sporty; the second is the employee who leaks the company's misdeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound names both an official signalling fouls and a worker who publicly exposes their organisation's misconduct.

clue.text: God! One who might shaft his enemies as a contender-for a capital administrator

parts.note: the Lord is God

parts.words: One who might shaft his enemies
parts.note: an archer fires shafts, that is arrows, at foes

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disbelief at a ruthless schemer standing to run London.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and Tory peer, sought to be Mayor of London before a perjury scandal ended his bid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservative peer was his party's candidate to become Mayor of London in 1999.

clue.text: 'Germans f off!': Al-Fayed's foreign accommodation

indicators.note: off means removed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: Fritz is a dated slang term for Germans collectively
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rude shout telling Germans to clear off from Mohamed Al-Fayed's hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'f off' looks like an expletive but is an instruction to drop the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohamed Al-Fayed owned the Ritz hotel in Paris, a lodging abroad from his London base.

clue.text: Against being hugged by archdeacon transsexual

indicators.note: being hugged by means held inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A scandal sheet's tale of a cleric embracing a trans person.
explanation.definitionFit: Contra is Latin for opposed to, used in English as in 'pros and contras'.

clue.text: See 21
Our bizarre stories of rich Europe compared with America?

parts.note: rich means laughable, as in 'that's rich', so funny
Europe is the Old World, set against the New World of the Americas

explanation.surface: Private Eye pointing to its own column of odd tales from wealthy Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Funny Old World is a Private Eye column collecting strange news items, hence 'Our'.
explanation.definitionFit: The magazine's long-running feature of weird news clippings bears this title.

clue.text: Such as 'Brillo Pad' can handle

parts.note: can and nick are both slang for prison
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A boast that a scouring pad can cope with any job.
explanation.walkthrough: Brillo Pad (or Brillo) is Private Eye's nickname for the editor Andrew Neil, after his wiry hair; Brillo pads are wire-wool scourers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is an informal or mocking name, like the Eye's label for Andrew Neil.

clue.text: A complete failure performed an after-dinner function

definitions.meaning: first meaning: finished and no longer successful, as of a has-been
second meaning: cleaned the dishes after the meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'after-dinner function' suggests a speech or banquet, but the job is doing the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone whose career is over, and also the past tense of cleaning plates after eating.

clue.text: Revered royal to wallop court, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, widely adored
wallop is British slang for beer, so ale

explanation.surface: A beloved princess seemingly about to strike a tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is old British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, a particular way of speaking.

clue.text: Group that leaves one in suspense without recourse to the law

definitions.text: Group that leaves one in suspense without recourse to the law

parts.words: Group that leaves one in suspense without recourse to the law
parts.note: suspense is literal: a crowd that hangs a victim without trial

explanation.walkthrough: 'in suspense' sounds like nervous waiting, but it means hanging from a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob that executes someone, usually by hanging, outside any legal process.

clue.text: American jerk on amphetamines

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to yank is to jerk sharply
E is slang for ecstasy, an amphetamine-type drug, so two of them are EE

explanation.surface: An insult about a speed-fuelled American idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal term for a person from the United States.

clue.text: Reveal some bum that's beneath a church member!

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath means the second piece goes below the first

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare buttocks
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone baring their backside under a member of a church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moonie is a follower of Sun Myung Moon's Unification Church.

clue.text: Community benefits from friendly masses?

parts.note: social means sociable or friendly
masses are church services

explanation.surface: A suggestion that welfare comes from kindly crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masses' looks like crowds of people but is the plural of Mass, the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Social services are publicly provided welfare help such as care for children and the elderly.

clue.text: Appendix snipped and wrapped in blubber is disgustingly useless

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to blubber is to cry noisily
the word appendix cut short to its abbreviation app.

explanation.surface: A grim medical scene: an appendix removed and wrapped in fat, a useless organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like body fat, but it is the verb meaning to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Crappy is vulgar slang for very poor quality or worthless.

clue.text: One gets mounted in a short time

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'
on means mounted, as in 'on horseback'

explanation.surface: A smutty remark that someone will soon be ridden.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic word meaning soon or shortly.

clue.text: Invigorating air needed by someone bonking — alarmingly, it's being depleted

parts.note: ozone is used loosely for fresh, bracing sea air
a layer is someone who lays, slang for having sex; bonking is British slang for it

explanation.surface: Fresh air needed by an exhausted lover who is running out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonking is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratospheric shield against ultraviolet rays has been thinning because of CFC pollution.

clue.text: Lapsed feminist to the point when gobbling one?

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: germane means relevant, to the point
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lewd jibe about a former feminist performing a sex act.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer, author of The Female Eunuch, was seen by Private Eye as having strayed from feminist orthodoxy.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer, the Australian writer, is the feminist icon whose later views drew criticism.

clue.text: Self important, having experienced an erection? Shame!

parts.note: up, as in aroused
'what a shame' and 'what a pity' mean the same

explanation.surface: A pompous man mocked for being aroused, with a cry of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity means arrogant or presumptuous, acting above one's station.
